## Ask Your Notes 1.3.0

This release makes note conversations easier to set up and more reliable, with live Obsidian theme support, a new note-and-conversation identity, and updated English and Chinese documentation.

### Highlights

- First-run connection guidance, reading/generation status, and an explicit @ button for choosing notes.
- Theme-aware backgrounds, text, accent colors, fonts, icons, and main control radii. Updated logo and light/dark README previews.
- Improved Markdown tables and code blocks, visible reply actions, keyboard-accessible references, and narrow-sidebar layouts.
- Request locking and session isolation prevent duplicate requests and stale replies after starting a new chat.
- Stopping a non-streaming request immediately ends local waiting and ignores late results. The underlying provider request may continue.
- Correct handling of empty unsaved editors, disabled automatic context, renamed/deleted references, and context-read errors.
- More reliable streaming parsing, serialized settings/history writes, preserved input drafts, and visible context truncation.
- Switching providers clears the previous API key; disabling history persistence clears saved history.

### Compatibility and data

- Requires Obsidian 1.15.0 or later, matching the minimum version verified for this release. Older releases retain their previous minimum versions.
- API keys are stored as plain text in local plugin data. Referenced notes and chat messages are sent to the endpoint you configure.
- This is a GitHub release; community-directory listing is a separate submission.

### Install

Download `main.js`, `manifest.json`, and `styles.css` from the assets below and place them in `<vault>/.obsidian/plugins/ask-your-notes/`, then reload and enable the plugin. Existing BRAT users can update through BRAT.

### Validation

- Production build and 14 regression tests pass.
- Desktop verification in Obsidian 1.15.0 covers themes, narrow layout, streaming, stopping, and request-error recovery. Mobile has not been verified on a physical device.
